'''Meenakshi Narain''' (May 9, 1964 – January 1, 2023) was an Indian-born American experimental physicist. She was a Professor of Physics and Chair of the Department of Physics at [[Brown University]], and was also Chair of the Collaboration Board of U.S. institutions in the [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] (CMS) Collaboration. She contributed to the discovery of the [[top quark]] in 1995 and [[Higgs boson|Higgs Boson]] in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |author1=Cern |date=2023-03-01 |title=Meenakshi Narain 1964–2023 |url=https://cerncourier.com/a/meenakshi-narain-1964-2023/ |access-date=2023-03-16 |website=CERN Courier |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Born on May 9, 1964,<ref name="obit"/> in [[Gorakhpur]], [[Uttar Pradesh]], India, Narain identified as an Asian-Indian American. In high school, she had to transfer to another all-girls school to study on the math track that led her to physics and statistics as an undergraduate. She had to overcome the family expectation to choose physics over law.<ref>{{Cite web |title=My Journey as a Physicist: Prof. Meenakshi Narain (She/Her): Season 2 Episode 7|url=https://sites.google.com/msu.edu/phy480905/season-2-snowmass#h.39lw8go0mxnb|author=Huey-Wen Lin|author2=Bryan Stanley|access-date=April 8, 2023|website=My Journey as a Physicist Podcast}}</ref> She completed a B.Sc. at [[Gorakhpur University]] and a M.Sc. at [[IIT Kanpur]]. Narain earned her Ph.D. at [[Stony Brook University]] with her dissertation titled, ''Inclusive Photon Spectra from Upsilon States'',<ref>{{Cite book |last=Narain |first=Meenakshi |title=Inclusive Photon Spectra from Upsilon States |publisher=State University of New York, Stony Brook |year=1991}}</ref> under the supervision of [[Juliet Lee-Franzini]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Physics Tree - Meenakshi Narain|url=https://academictree.org/physics/peopleinfo.php?pid=138477|access-date=September 13, 2021|website=academictree.org}}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:Meenakshi Narain with torch.png|thumb|left|Brown Physics Professor and organizer of the Big Bang Science Fair, Meenakshi Narain, lights the WaterFire.]]
Following her doctorate, Narain was a visiting fellow at the Laboratory of Nuclear Studies, [[Cornell University]], and then as a post-doc at [[Fermilab|Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory]] from 1991–1995, where she was also a Wilson Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Fermilab {{!}} For Physicists & Engineers {{!}} Fellowships |url=https://www.fnal.gov/pub/forphysicists/fellowships/robert_wilson/past.html |access-date=July 21, 2022 |website=www.fnal.gov}}</ref>

Narain was on the faculty of [[Boston University]] for eight years prior to joining the [[Brown University]] faculty in 2007,<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 25, 2018 |title=Meenakshi Narain: A Physicist Working With Particle Accelerators and Helping Discover the Higgs Boson |url=https://indianewengland.com/2018/05/meenakshi-narain-a-physicist-working-with-particle-accelerators-and-helping-discover-the-higgs-boson/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210913031754/https://indianewengland.com/2018/05/meenakshi-narain-a-physicist-working-with-particle-accelerators-and-helping-discover-the-higgs-boson/ |archive-date=September 13, 2021 |access-date=September 13, 2021 |website=INDIA New England News |language=en |quote=Presently, Ms. Narain is co-leading the effort to establish the vision for opportunities at the collider in year 2023 and beyond.  Narain is engaged in research and development towards the construction of the innermost part of detector using silicon sensors. Her research also deals with the analysis of large data sets and provides an excellent training ground for students in data science.}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Kwon |first=Diana |title=Big Bang Science Fair at WaterFire Providence |url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/big-bang-science-fair-at-waterfire-providence |access-date=September 13, 2021 |website=symmetry magazine |date=September 17, 2019 |language=en |quote=My vision is to make people appreciate science in the same way they appreciate art and music," Narain says. "If we can make people feel that science is a fun thing to do, learn and converse about, I think that could be a way to change our society.}}</ref> where she was promoted to full professor in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 - Physics at Brown |url=https://studylib.net/doc/18653210/2010---physics-at-brown |access-date=July 22, 2022 |website=studylib.net |page=7 |language=en}}</ref> Her research activities have included the [[DØ experiment]] at [[Fermilab]]. She was instrumental in the discovery of the [[top quark]] in 1995.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Staley |first1=Kent W. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=a69Dp9V0wBEC&dq=%22Meenakshi+Narain%22+-wikipedia&pg=PA188 |title=The Evidence for the Top Quark: Objectivity and Bias in Collaborative Experimentation |last2=Staley |first2=Staley, Kent Wade |date=April 5, 2004 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-82710-2 |page=188 |language=en}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Sundermier |first=Ali |title=How to make a discovery |url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/how-to-make-a-discovery |access-date=September 13, 2021 |website=symmetry magazine |date=March 28, 2017 |language=en |quote=Narain's groups analysis was essential to the collaboration’s understanding of a signal that turned out to be the elusive top quark.}}</ref>

Narain participated in the [[Compact Muon Solenoid|CMS experiment]] at the [[Large Hadron Collider]] at [[CERN]], and  contributed to the discovery [[Higgs boson|Higgs Boson]] in 2012.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news |last=Heilprin |first=John |date=July 3, 2012 |title=Physicists ready data on 'God particle' to explain everything |pages=A4 |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/105810890/physicists-ready-data-on-god-particle/ |access-date=July 18, 2022 |quote=Meenakshi Narain, a physics professor at Brown University who works on one of the teams, said that although she could not disclose what will be announced on Wednesday, this was a "once in a lifetime event," because the experiments have provided enough data to give "at least the first hints of it in a significant way," or to rule out the existence of Higgs.}}</ref> She served as Chair of the Collaboration Board of U.S. institutions in the [[Compact Muon Solenoid]] (CMS) Collaboration from July 2018 to July 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Professor Narain Elected US CMS Collaboration Board Chair {{!}} Physics {{!}} Brown University |url=https://www.brown.edu/academics/physics/news/2018/06/professor-narain-elected-us-cms-collaboration-board-chair |access-date=September 13, 2021 |website=www.brown.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Narain, Meenakshi |url=https://vivo.brown.edu/display/mnarain |access-date=September 13, 2021 |website=vivo.brown.edu}}</ref>

Narain was a frequent advocate for women in [[Science, technology, engineering, and mathematics|STEM]] fields,<ref>{{Cite web|last=Chen|first=Frances|date=April 22, 2015|title=Female academics combat bias in STEM fields|url=https://www.browndailyherald.com/2015/04/22/female-academics-combat-bias-in-stem-fields/|access-date=September 13, 2021|website=Brown Daily Herald|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Faculty, students reflect on STEM faculty gender gap |url=https://www.browndailyherald.com/article/2022/04/faculty-students-reflect-on-stem-faculty-gender-gap |access-date=July 22, 2022 |website=The Brown Daily Herald |language=en-US}}</ref> and she also promoted science to the general public, in events such as the WaterFire Big Bang Science Fair in [[Providence, Rhode Island]].<ref name=":2" />
